primitives.name: Content Delivery Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: A "content delivery network" or "content distribution network" (CDN) generally refers to a distributed content delivery system that comprises a collection of computers or computing devices linked by a network or networks.
primitives.assumptions: Network topology is static; content is uniformly distributed across nodes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When node failure exceeds threshold D/2, latency increases exponentially.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Models CDN as a probabilistic graph for content routing. GSE: Treats CDN as a reactive state machine with load-dependent transitions.

primitives.name: Ad Serving Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: An ad server 130 comprises a server that stores online advertisements for presentation to users.
primitives.assumptions: Ads are served in real-time with minimal delay; user behavior is predictable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T_a > 500ms, ad relevance drops below threshold.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Models ad serving as a stochastic process with reward maximization. GSE: Treats ad serving as a temporal logic state transition governed by user engagement.
layer2.telemetry: Click-through rate, revenue per impression, auction timing

primitives.name: Content Server Infrastructure
primitives.verbatim_quote: The content server 106 may include a device that includes a configuration to provide content via a network to another device.
primitives.assumptions: Server load scales linearly with user count; content is stored in memory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When U > S/L, system enters overload state.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Models server load as a queueing system. GSE: Treats server as a stateful actor with input/output buffering.
layer2.telemetry: Storage utilization, response time, concurrent users

The system assumes uniform node distribution and static topology. When node failure exceeds D/2, the system enters a high-latency regime due to re-routing. Ad serving mechanism (ASM) functions as a real-time stochastic process where A ads are matched with user U based on T_a. If T_a exceeds 500ms, ad relevance degrades. Content server infrastructure (CSI) models server load as a function of U and S, where L increases with U/S. These primitives interconnect through shared telemetry metrics such as latency and throughput, forming a dual system of content and monetization.
